checks.name: Binding completeness
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test protocols binding_completeness:: && rustc --edition 2024 --emit=metadata --extern automonique_protocol=rust/target/debug/libautomonique_protocol.rlib -L dependency=rust/target/debug/deps - (ClientBindingParts literal with the actor field omitted)
checks.output: 5 tests pass. Every binding reads back dialect, actor, granted scopes, quotas and credential revision; an empty client id and an empty scope set are each refused; granted scopes are deduplicated so one scope cannot be counted twice; and each of the dialects reaches the domain as an ordinary scoped actor. I compiled a ClientBindingParts literal with the actor field omitted and rustc rejected it with error[E0063] (missing field `actor`), so the tenant-free binding compile_fail in the module docs fails for the intended reason.

checks.name: Mapping injectivity
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test protocols mapping_injectivity::
checks.output: 8 tests pass. One external identifier never resolves to two canonical identities and never crosses canonical kinds; two external identifiers reach one canonical identity only through an explicit alias record; an alias of an unmapped primary is refused; an alias cannot retarget an identifier that is already mapped; rebinding the same pair is idempotent; injectivity is scoped per dialect and per client; and an unmapped identifier refuses rather than inventing an identity.

checks.name: No alternate state
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test protocols no_alternate_state:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc
checks.output: 8 tests pass. A projection reads canonical state rather than a copy (a reprojection of a revised value reports the new title and revision), its dialect is read back out of the binding, two projections of one state are equal including their projected output so neither mints a session, cursor or approval of its own, and the type's width is asserted to be exactly its two shared borrows rather than left to prose. Every effect a projection offers lands in CanonicalActionKind::ALL and carries the binding's own actor; withholding each action's required scope in turn makes exactly that action fail, so no scope grants another and there is no alternate authorization policy. The compile_fail coverage runs in the doc suite (69 doctests pass: 27 standalone, 42 merged) and includes the lifetime tie that stops a projection outliving the canonical value.

checks.name: Effect equivalence
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test protocols effect_equivalence:: idempotency_scoping::
checks.output: 6 + 5 tests pass. Every ExternalOperation maps to exactly one CanonicalActionKind and reaches the action it declares; a plan carries its idempotency key and expected revision and a plan without a key is refused; a duplicate external request yields the same receipt; one idempotency key cannot be reused for a different target. The scoping tests are the sharper half: two tenants sharing a key do not collide, two canonical actions on one target do not collapse into one receipt, a separator inside a tenant or inside a caller key cannot forge another actor's ledger key, and a key with no separator keeps its spelling unchanged.

checks.name: Approval fidelity
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test protocols approval_fidelity:: && rustc --edition 2024 --emit=metadata ... - (ApprovalTarget::Everything and HostApprovalDecision::BypassAll)
checks.output: 4 tests pass: each host answer maps to one distinct typed decision, an approval names exactly one provider or one tool, the exact target revision survives the mapping, and only a resolved tenant actor decides an approval. I compiled `ApprovalTarget::Everything` and `HostApprovalDecision::BypassAll` directly; both were rejected with error[E0599] (no variant), so the two global-bypass compile_fail doctests fail for the intended reason rather than incidentally.

checks.name: Honest degradation
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test protocols honest_degradation::
checks.output: 9 tests pass. Every dialect declares every semantic exactly once, so the capability table is total; the declared cell is the outcome the client actually receives and each declared cell is the one under review; an unsupported semantic returns a typed error rather than being dropped; a degraded semantic carries bounded text plus the link to the authoritative record; over-long text is truncated and marked rather than silently shortened; an unusable rendering is refused rather than emitted empty; the authoritative record is asserted intact across degradation; and only the native surface represents everything. There is no ProjectedSemantic variant meaning 'omitted' -- the compile_fail for it is in the doc suite.

checks.name: Native escape hatch
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test protocols native_escape_hatch::
checks.output: 2 tests pass: every dialect can express a native resource link, and every successful projection carries the link, so a client whose own protocol cannot represent a semantic is pointed at the canonical surface rather than served an approximation.

checks.name: Remote claims carry nothing
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test protocols remote_claims_carry_nothing::
checks.output: 3 tests pass: a remote claim never resolves to an Actor, it cannot supply a scope the binding lacks, and attaching one does not change the plan it travels with. RemoteAgentClaim has no actor() accessor -- the compile_fail asserting that is in the doc suite.

checks.name: Range coexistence
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test protocols range_coexistence::
checks.output: 6 tests pass: each binding declares a supported range, an inverted range is refused, adjacent releases coexist on their overlap, an in-range client may mutate, an incompatible client is admitted read-only and keeps reading, and every unsupported mutation fails closed naming both versions. Planning a mutation requires a MutationAuthority that only the in-range admission branch produces, so the read-only client has nothing to attempt a mutation with.
